findings.claim: The plan's verification tiers silently drop the Flutter halves of two blocking constraints, leaving 'affected companion gates' as the only coverage and making it ambiguous whether flutter analyze/test ever runs.
findings.evidence: Constraints build-passes and invariant-tests-pass are blocking and include 'flutter analyze mobile' and 'flutter test mobile', but the plan's T2 tier states only 'Rust workspace tests/build, web build and architecture audit, plus affected companion gates' — no change in the 22-item list touches mobile/, so 'affected' can be read as excluding the Flutter gates entirely from every tier (T0, T1, T2, T3).
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly in the tier definitions that the blocking constraint commands (cargo build/test --workspace, pnpm --dir web build, flutter analyze mobile, flutter test mobile, bash scripts/audit.sh) run at change-archive and phase completion regardless of which surface was touched, or name Flutter as an always-run companion gate in T2.

findings.claim: ra-19 acceptance criterion 3 contains a typo ('sQLite') that reads as a distinct term in a blocking disposition criterion.
findings.evidence: ra-19 acceptance 3: 'When parity, approved encryption/storage or a measured benefit is absent, sQLite release selection remains blocked and the tested PGlite baseline remains the candidate'.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct to 'SQLite release selection remains blocked' so the criterion names the engine unambiguously when it is copied into the OpenSpec spec delta.
